sam (infra): Heads-up — planning a short maintenance in eu-central to swap a handful of older A100 nodes with refreshed instances and apply NIC firmware that fixes the flapping egress counters. Target window: 2026-04-02 02:00-04:00 UTC.
lia (oncall): +1. What's the plan for draining? we have high-priority Dedicated clusters there.
sam (infra): Strategy: staggered pool-level drains of ~10 nodes at a time, 15m drain each, 10m cool-down, then backfill into eu-central-backup (cheaper prewarmed pool in same AZ). We'll keep 2 warm racks for Dedicated customers.
danika (capacity): can we avoid cross-region backfill? egress costs spiked last time when we spilled to us-west.
sam (infra): yes — prefer intra-region backfill first. only if pool utilization > 85% do we route to other regions. That threshold is configurable in the autoscaler policy.
dmitri: note: the NIC firmware patch forces a short link reset per host. networking team measured ~5s of packet loss during apply. app-level fallbacks should cover that, but we should avoid simultaneous reboots on nodes that share the same TOR switch.
ops-bot: Incident sched created: MAINT-4382 — "eu-central: node swaps + nic fw" scheduled for 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC. Pager rotation: lia -> remi.
lia (oncall): I'll own runbook execution. Sam — can you paste the drain commands you'll use so I can sanity-check?
sam (infra): sure:
```
# drain sequence (per-node)
kubectl drain node/<node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
# after pod eviction and eviction check, mark node for firmware update
ssh gpuadmin@<node> sudo /usr/local/bin/nic-fw-update --staged; sudo reboot
```
lia (oncall): ok. add a `sleep 15` between steps to avoid simultaneous TOR flaps. and add a pre-check for disk pressure: `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[?(@.metadata.name=="<node>")].status.conditions[*].type}'`
anika (capacity): capacity note: we'll reserve 8 v100-equivalent slots from the eu-central-backup pool during the window to keep p99 latency for Dedicated. that increases cost but avoids customer impact. estimated incremental cost ~€420 for the window. Is that approved?
remi: finance — that's acceptable given SLA windows, confirm with product ops?
sam (infra): product ops verbal OK for emergency patching. I'll make the cost explicit in the post-mortem.
dmitri: monitoring checklist:
- dashboard: infra/eu-central/gpu-pool-health (watch p99 latency, queue depth)
- network: net/eu-central/egress-errors (watch flapping counter)
- autoscaler: events stream for cross-region-schedule
- alert: if backfill > 10 nodes to other regions, escalate to eng-ops
lia (oncall): I'll set one-off overrides to temporarily raise the autoscaler threshold to 92% if we see unnecessary cross-region movement.
sam (infra): rollout plan:
1) notify customers with Dedicated in eu-central (maint email + console banner 48h before)
2) prewarm backup pool 1h before window
3) run small canary: drain 2 nodes, validate canaries (p50/p95) for 20m
4) proceed in 10-node batches with 10m cooldown between batches
5) once all nodes swapped, run cluster healthcheck script and keep warm racks for 4h

lia (oncall): can we add a canary that includes a large-embedding job? that was the worst-case from last time.
sam (infra): good call — include a synthetic embedding load and a small multi-request chat workload. I'll add the job to canary playbook.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: prewarm job queued to eu-central-backup at 2026-04-02T01:00:00Z
remi: communications: draft posted to #customer-notifications, I'll push once you confirm. include rollback notes and expected impact: short ephemeral increase in p99 latency for non-Dedicated workloads; Dedicated unaffected by default.
anika (capacity): one more cost trade: if we extend cooldown from 10m to 20m we reduce transient queue spikes but increase reserve time and cost. recommendation: keep 10m, but add dynamic throttling on egress to limit cross-region bursting.
dmitri: how do we throttle egress quickly? kernel-level shaping or kube-proxy rate-limit?
sam (infra): we'll use region egress policer in our loadbalancer (fast to flip) — set to 400Mbps per-rack for the swap window. ops-bot will flip flag during sequence.
lia (oncall): assigned actions: Sam -> finalize runbook and add `sleep` tweaks; Anika -> reserve backup pool and confirm cost; Remi -> customer comms + post; Dmitri -> validate net policer and TOR sequencing; Lia -> runbook lead during window.
sam (infra): thanks. I'll post final checklist here 24h before start. If anyone wants to be on the war room, ping me. :phone: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: MAINT-4382 status: planned -> ready_for_maintenance
remi: added docs link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eu-central-nic-firmware-swap
lia (oncall): copying the command we'll use to check in-flight evictions: `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -n redwood-system -o wide`
sam (infra): cool. see you all in the war room if needed.
